FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Engineering Metrology Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Councrl. Dial snap gauge is a handy equipment for indicative measurement of the components. It may be applied to the work in the machine or may be gripped in one hand and the workpiece fed into it. The standard is based on the manufacturing practices prevailing in the country.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the resuit of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

This standard covers the functional requirements of dial snap gauges in the range of 0 to 300 mm, which can be used with suitable dial indicator with least count of 0.00 lmm. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provision of this standard. 6 MATERIAL AND HARDNESS 6.1 The frame of the dial snap gauge shall be made of aluminium alloy or equivalent material which will ensure light design and stability. 6.2 The anvils oc the dial snap gauge shall be made from materials given in IS 7018 ( Part 1 ) : 1983 or can be tipped with carbide or an; other kquivalent material. 6.3 The spindles of the dial snap gauge shall be made from materials given in IS : 7018 ( Part 1 ) : 1983.
2

6.4 The material of other parts of the dial snap gauge shall be of good quality and free from flaws. 6.5 Hardness of anvil and spindle shall not be less than 700 i-N 7 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 7.1 The design of frame of the dial snap gauge shall be convenient to handle and easy to use.
the dial

7.2 The sensing spindle and adjustable spindle of snap gauge shall have sufficient bearing

IS 14271 : 1995

length on their shank to ensure parallel movement while being adjusted and to obviate any tendency to trip when being locked or when in use. Sliding anvil shall be of close fitting 7.3 All parts of dial snap gauges shall be free from sharp corners. 7.4 Dial snap gauges shall have a collet chuck for fixing of dial indicator/digital dial gauge of 8 mm dial stem. 7.5 Arrangement for fixing the dial gauge shall be such as to ensure rigidity in clamping and alignment with the measuring axis to meet or exceed the accuracy requirement of the dial calliper as given in 9. This shall be suitable for clamping of all dials with 8H6 stem diameter. Fixing arrangement shall not damage the stem. 7.6 Dial gauge protector shall be of robust design to provide adequate protection to the dial gauge and shall preferably be made of steel. 7.7 Sensing spindle shall be closely guided in bush to maintain parallelism throughout the travel as specified in 9. 7.8 Adjusting spindle shall be closely guided in bush to maintain parallelism as specified in 9 when locked in any part of measuring range. 7.9 Stopper shall be rigid enough to ensure same contact point of sliding and adjusting anvil repeatedly. 7.10 Insulation grip shall be made of suitable insulating material such as plastic or its equivalent and shall be designed to ensure good grip while handling. 7.11 Adjustment locking nut shall be designed such that it shall not disturb the parallelism of
Table 2 Permissible

adjusting anvil throughout the range and shall lock firmly to maintain size during use. 7.12 Adjusting nut shall move freely and uniformly, by thumb, throughout the adjustment range. 8 SETTING Setting of dial snap gauge either by slip gauge or by means of setting plug is recommended. Final locking in position should be done by means of adjustment locking nut. 9 ACCURACY
AND SURFACE FINISH 9.1 The eiror in flatness of measuring faces shall

not exceed .0015 mm.
9.2 The error in parallelism of measuring faces shall not exceed the values given in Table 2.

9.3 The roughness value (R,) of measuring faces shall not exceed 0.1 pm. 10 DESIGNATION
10.1 Dial snap No., range and gauge of range designated as: Dial snap

gauge shall be designated by IS grade. For example, a dial snap 50-70 mm and Grade 1 shall be gauge IS 14271 50-75 Gr 1

12 PRESERVATION AND PACKING 12.1 Each dial snap gauge shall be coated with suitable anti-corrosive coating on working surface of anvil and other important surfaces. 12.2 Dial snap gauge shall be supplied in suitable protective case.
